title: Putting Greens in Northeast Florida | TIMELESS Grass & Greens
description: Backyard putting greens from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine Shores. Choose the shape, cups and fringe with a free visit, layout and written estimate.
h1: Putting greens in northeast Florida, built around the shots you practice.
lede: Short putts by the patio or longer lines across the yard, with cups placed clear of your walkways. We measure at a free visit, then give a written price.
wins: Shape the green around your practice goals
Consider shade, drainage and the rest of the yard
Choose cups, fringe and finishing before work begins

answer.question: How do I plan a putting green in a Florida yard?
answer.answer: Start with the shots you practice, then fit them to the site: sun, falling leaves, where rain gathers and any association rules. We measure the space at a free visit, then give a written price.

blocks.h2: Build around the shots you enjoy.
blocks.takeaway: Build the green around the putts and approach shots you actually practice, with cup positions that don't crowd the yard's routes. A fringe or chipping area is a layout choice to price beforehand.
paras: A green can focus on short putts near the patio or offer several lines across a larger area. Tell us how you practice and where you want to stand. Cup positions and contours should make the space useful without crowding the routes through the yard.

For chipping, include the approach area and intended direction of play when we discuss the design. The space and selected turf system need to suit those shots. A fringe or separate chipping area is a layout choice to price before work begins.

blocks.h2: Consider the surface through the day.
blocks.takeaway: Walk the spot at the time you'd use it: direct sun can make turf hot, and nearby trees drop leaves onto the green. Point out where water gathers after rain.
paras: Walk the proposed area when you are likely to use it. Direct sun can make turf hot, so consider nearby shade and where you will stand between shots. Trees also bring leaves and other debris that need clearing from the putting surface.

Point out water that gathers after rain and how runoff leaves the yard. A base that shapes the green still needs a workable drainage plan. Review the base and underlying ground as well as the way water leaves the proposed area.

blocks.h2: Check the layout before selecting materials.
blocks.takeaway: On an association property, bring its landscape requirements and mark where the green will sit, including what's visible from nearby lots and common areas. Ask which rules cover the base, turf and infill you're choosing.
paras: For an association property, bring the applicable landscape requirements and identify the proposed green’s location. Check visibility from nearby property and common areas when resolving the approval question.

The product and installation must also fit the rules that apply to the property. Ask which requirements cover the proposed base, turf and infill. Our Florida turf guide and HOA guide address those questions without replacing a review of your layout.

blocks.h2: Choose the finished roll and the work behind it.
blocks.takeaway: Size, access, removal, base shaping, cups and fringe shape the price, while the surface, infill and brushing shape the roll. It needs no irrigation to grow, but cleaning takes time and may use water.
paras: Size, access, removal, base shaping, cup positions and fringe all affect the installation price. We draw the proposed layout after the free visit so you can review the choices together.

The putting surface, infill and brushing influence the roll. Ask how the selected system is adjusted and cared for, then keep leaves and debris off the green and inspect the edges. A synthetic green needs no irrigation for growth, but cleaning still uses time and may use water. See the putting-green options before your visit.

faq.q: Can the green go near the patio?
faq.a: Include the patio edge, walking routes and where people sit in the drawing. The free visit is where we discuss transitions and the space needed for the putts or chips you want to practice.

faq.q: Can I change the layout of an existing green?
faq.a: Describe the changes you want and any problems with the current surface. Moving cups or changing contours may involve work below the turf, so those choices need to be included in the replacement scope.

faq.q: How much routine attention does it need?
faq.a: Clear debris and follow the selected product’s brushing, cleaning and infill guidance. Assess changes in roll or loose edges before deciding whether adjustment, infill or repair is needed.
